United Nations S/RES/1751 (2007) Security Council Distr.: General 13 April 2007

Resolution 1751 (2007) Adopted by the Security Council at its 5660th meeting, on 13 April 2007

The Security Council, Recalling its resolutions and the statements of its President concerning the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Reaffirming its commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and its commitment to continue to contribute to the consolidation of peace and stability in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the post-transition period, in particular through the United Nations Organization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUC), Noting that the situation in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to pose a threat to international peace and security in the region, Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations,

1. Decides to extend the mandate and personnel strength of MONUC, as set out in its resolutions 1565 (2004), 1592 (2005), 1596 (2005), 1621 (2005), 1635 (2005) and 1736 (2006), until 15 May 2007;

2. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.
